_comment: The misconceptions Cambridge Primary Science names for Stage 1, one per row of the 'Common misconceptions' table in each of the 24 topics of the Teacher's Resource. Ground truth for the misconception arm of science/lesson-kit/check-coverage.py: a Stage 1 step cites ids from here in its `mis` list, the gate fails an id nothing cites and a citation this file does not hold. `misconception` states the false idea a child holds; `overcome` is this repo's one-line summary of the corrective move, not the Teacher's Resource's wording. `lesson` is the Grade 1 standalone lesson that must answer it - the eight lessons are organised by 0097 sub-strand, so one lesson answers several Cambridge topics.
source: Cambridge Primary Science Teacher's Resource 1 (Board & Cross), Common misconceptions, topics 1.1-6.5
_minimumCovered: Raised to the measured value when the depth pass lands; coverage is a number that only goes up. A parser that stops recognising one lesson's citations otherwise takes a whole lesson out of the comparison while the gate still prints a tick.

misconceptions.misconception: Clouds, water and fire are alive, because they move and grow.
misconceptions.overcome: Moving is not the test. Clouds and water are moved by the wind and need no food; fire needs no water.

misconceptions.misconception: Water and the Sun are alive, because plants need water and light to grow.
misconceptions.overcome: Helping a living thing to live does not make a thing alive. A biscuit keeps you alive and is not alive.

misconceptions.misconception: Plants are not alive, because they do not move about.
misconceptions.overcome: Plants grow, take in water, make their own food and make seeds. That is enough to be alive.

misconceptions.misconception: The word plant means flowers and shrubs only; a tree or grass is something else.
misconceptions.overcome: Plant covers every mostly green living thing that makes its own food, trees and grass included.

misconceptions.misconception: The roots suck up the plant's food.
misconceptions.overcome: The roots take in water. The food is made in the leaves.

misconceptions.misconception: The whole plant is called a flower; the flower is not recognised as one part.
misconceptions.overcome: The flower is one part. A plant with no flower on it today is still a plant.

misconceptions.misconception: A plant must have light from the Sun; only sunlight will do.
misconceptions.overcome: Plants need light. Light from a lamp works too, which is how plants grow well indoors.

misconceptions.misconception: Plants need to be given food, the way a pet does.
misconceptions.overcome: A plant makes its own food in its leaves. Shop plant food only helps it stay healthy.

misconceptions._lesson: Lesson 1 holds the water experiment (Does a plant need water?); lesson 2's experiment is the light one. 1.4-m2 stays in lesson 2, where the roots are taught.
misconceptions.misconception: Every plant needs a lot of water every single day.
misconceptions.overcome: Plants outside do not get rain every day, and soil in a pot stays damp for several days.

misconceptions.misconception: Water goes into a plant through its leaves.
misconceptions.overcome: The roots take the water in from the soil.

misconceptions.misconception: Sound cannot go around corners.
misconceptions.overcome: You can hear something you cannot see, from behind a door or round a corner.

misconceptions.misconception: Sound only travels through air.
misconceptions.overcome: Sound travels through a wall, and through water - a swimmer underwater still hears.

misconceptions.misconception: A sound only travels to the person listening to it.
misconceptions.overcome: A sound spreads out everywhere at once. Everyone standing round it can hear it.

misconceptions.misconception: A quiet sound is not really a sound; only loud things make sounds.
misconceptions.overcome: The quietest tap on a drum is still a sound. Quiet sounds are sounds.

misconceptions.misconception: You only hear something if you are listening for it.
misconceptions.overcome: A sound at night can wake you, which proves your ears work while you sleep.

misconceptions.misconception: A sound heard from far away was a quieter sound when it was made.
misconceptions.overcome: The source made the same sound. It got quieter on the way to you.

misconceptions.misconception: Material means cloth.
misconceptions.overcome: In science, material means whatever a thing is made of - wood, metal, glass, rock, all of it.

misconceptions.misconception: Soft and smooth mean the same thing.
misconceptions.overcome: Soft means it squashes. Smooth means it is not bumpy. A sponge is soft and not smooth.

misconceptions.misconception: The name of the object is the name of the material.
misconceptions.overcome: A spoon is the object; metal is the material. Ask what it is made of, not what it is.

misconceptions.misconception: Groups can be made by mixing different kinds of property at once, so a thing ends up in two groups or none.
misconceptions.overcome: Pick one pair and keep it for the whole sort: bendy or stiff, rough or smooth, hard or soft.

misconceptions.misconception: Hard means difficult, so a hard material is a tricky one.
misconceptions.overcome: Hard has two meanings. Here it means not soft. Say difficult for the other one.

misconceptions.misconception: Anything bendy can also be stretched, squashed and twisted.
misconceptions.overcome: Paper squashes, twists and bends, and does not stretch. Test each change on its own.

misconceptions.misconception: Elastic means anything that can be stretched.
misconceptions.overcome: Elastic means it goes back to its old shape afterwards. A sponge does; paper does not.

misconceptions.misconception: A fair test means being fair to the children doing it, like taking turns.
misconceptions.overcome: A fair test is fair to the things being tested: change one thing and keep the rest the same.

misconceptions.misconception: The Earth is flat.
misconceptions.overcome: A globe and photographs taken from space show it is a ball.

misconceptions.misconception: The Earth is small - about as big as the places you know.
misconceptions.overcome: A plane flies for hours and crosses only a little of it. The part you live in is a speck on a globe.

misconceptions.misconception: The earth you dig in and the Earth we live on are the same word for the same thing.
misconceptions.overcome: Say planet Earth for the world, and soil for the stuff in the garden.

misconceptions.topicTitle: Heat and light from the Sun
misconceptions.misconception: Every bright light in the night sky is a star.
misconceptions.overcome: The Moon, a plane and the planets are bright too, and none of them is a star.

misconceptions.topicTitle: Heat and light from the Sun
misconceptions.misconception: The Earth stays still and the Sun goes round it.
misconceptions.overcome: The Sun stays still. The Earth turns, which makes the Sun look as if it moves.

misconceptions.misconception: Only a big lump is rock; sand is not rock.
misconceptions.overcome: Sand is rock broken into tiny pieces. A magnifier shows the same sharp, shiny grains.

misconceptions.misconception: Soil is just dirt, and worth nothing.
misconceptions.overcome: Seeds grow in soil, and all our food comes from plants. Soil is precious.

misconceptions.misconception: The loudest or biggest character in the room must be the tallest.
misconceptions.overcome: Stand back to back and measure. Measuring settles it; guessing does not.

misconceptions.misconception: Only your hands can feel touch.
misconceptions.overcome: All your skin feels touch. Someone can draw a shape on your back and you know what it was.

misconceptions.misconception: It is easier to say how people are different than how they are the same.
misconceptions.overcome: Look for the same things too: two eyes, two ears, hair, teeth. Everyone shares most of them.

misconceptions.misconception: Groups can be made by switching what you are sorting by half way through.
misconceptions.overcome: Give each group a name. If the names do not match, you changed what you were sorting by.

misconceptions.misconception: All twins look exactly the same.
misconceptions.overcome: Some twins look alike and some do not. A brother and sister can be twins.

misconceptions.misconception: Eating healthily means never eating a cake or a sweet again.
misconceptions.overcome: A little is fine. Cakes and sweets are a treat, not an every-day food.

misconceptions.misconception: A wrong prediction is a failure, so it is better to say you were right.
misconceptions.overcome: A wrong prediction is how you learn something new. Real scientists get them wrong too.

misconceptions.misconception: People are not animals.
misconceptions.overcome: In science, people are animals. You need air, water and food like every other animal.

misconceptions.misconception: Round things move on their own, because they are round.
misconceptions.overcome: A ball sits still until something pushes or pulls it, even on a slope.

misconceptions.misconception: A force you cannot feel is not a force.
misconceptions.overcome: Try turning a page with no force at all. Even a tiny move needs a push or a pull.

misconceptions.misconception: A tiny push or pull does not count as a force.
misconceptions.overcome: Sliding a sheet of paper is a push. Small forces are forces.

misconceptions.misconception: Anything that works must use electricity.
misconceptions.overcome: Look for a plug, a lead or a battery. No lead and no battery means no electricity.

misconceptions.misconception: Things float because they are small.
misconceptions.overcome: A big boat floats and a small glass marble sinks. Size is not what decides it.

misconceptions.misconception: Things only float in deep water.
misconceptions.overcome: The same things float in a shallow tray. Depth is not what decides it.

misconceptions.misconception: If no part of it is above the water, it has sunk.
misconceptions.overcome: Some things float low, just under the top. It has only sunk when it reaches the bottom.

misconceptions.misconception: A magnet has to be a red horseshoe to be a magnet.
misconceptions.overcome: Magnets come in bars, rings, discs and buttons, in any colour.

misconceptions.misconception: A magnet sticks to things.
misconceptions.overcome: Glue sticks. A magnet attracts - it pulls magnetic things towards it, and lets go again.
